newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest banks Q2 EPS seen up about 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest banks Q2 EPS seen up about 10 pct.

text.p: U.S. Midwest banks are expected to post second-quarter earnings per share that are on average 10 percent higher than in the same period a year ago.
Expense control measures and share repurchases are believed to have offset slowing loan growth and flat net interest margins.
"We've kind of gotten to the point where the expense controls and the share buybacks ... are even more important," Thomas Maier, a banking analyst at EVEREN Securities, said.
Maier and other analysts said net interest margins have been relatively flat and loan growth has slowed as the current economic expansion enters a more mature phase.
"This is late in the cycle, so you're not going to see a whole lot of loan growth," James Schutz, a banking analyst at ABN AMRO Chicago Corp, said.
Fee income from trust management, automatic teller machine networks and credit card operations are expected to help boost earnings, as in recent quarters.
"The outlook for fee income is generally better than the outlook in net interest income in my view," Schutz said. "Banks are handling those products well."
Among the Midwest banks expected to benefit from strong fee income are Northern Trust Corp, First Bank System Inc and Norwest Corp, analysts said.
While consumer loan growth appears to be slowing, credit card portfolios should begin stabilizing after months of deterioration for some companies, analysts said.
"Stock prices for companies like Banc One Corp ) and First Chicago NBD Corp are going to swing on credit card (performance)," Michael Ancell, an analyst at Edward D. Jones, said.

Still, Banc One is expected to post a slight decline in earnings per share in the second quarter, according to the First Call mean estimate. The company has said it expected some dilution from its recent acquisition of First USA.
The following are the First Call mean estimates for second-quarter earnings, compared with earnings for the second quarter of 1996:
Banc One $0.77 $0.80
Firstar Corp $0.52 $0.48
First Bank System $1.31 $1.17
First Chicago $1.20 $1.09
KeyCorp $1.01 $0.92
Magna Group Inc $0.58 $0.54
Mercantile Bancorp Inc $1.02 $0.94
National City Corp $0.89 $0.81
Northern Trust $0.63 $0.54
Norwest $0.86 $0.76
Note: Marshall & Ilsley Corp on Tuesday said second-quarter earnings rose to $0.58 a share on a diluted basis from $0.50 in the year-earlier period.
